title: Capacity reintegration playbook — PRD draft
summary: Proposal for a staging-friendly reintegration system: controlled reintroduction of tenants after burst/quarantine or soft-eviction, coordinated with autoscaler behavior and isolation policies to reduce oscillation and SLA impact.
content:
OVERVIEW

This is a working PRD sketch for a 'capacity reintegration' playbook for Dedicated pools. We want a pragmatic system that safely brings tenants back from ephemeral isolation (quarantine, soft-eviction, headroom-shedding) without causing capacity thrash or repeated SLA violations. Focus areas: orchestration semantics, autoscaler coordination, tenant health signals, and small API/console surfaces for operators and customers.

Why a separate playbook?
- We already have burst/credit and soft-eviction concepts across many docs. What is missing is a prescriptive, operational flow for reintegration that: (a) is conservative by default to avoid ping-pong, (b) exposes configurable knobs for enterprise tenants, (c) interacts cleanly with predictive autoscalers and warm pools.

PROBLEM STATEMENT
- When tenants are quarantined (e.g., noisy neighbor), or when we soft-evict to protect latency SLOs, reintroducing them naively often causes immediate re-triggering of the same protections. That leads to oscillation, degraded UX, and wasted warm-starts.
- Autoscalers and warm pools currently treat reintegration as normal traffic; they don’t know the tenant is in a probationary state. This misses an opportunity to shape the reintegration ramp.
- Operators lack a small set of clear metrics and actions to verify safe reintegration for an individual tenant.

GOALS
- Provide a deterministic reintegration flow that reduces oscillations by 50% in our simulated noisy-neighbor scenarios.
- Offer tenant-facing configuration (sensible defaults) for reintegration aggressiveness: conservative | balanced | aggressive.
- Minimize end-user SLA impact during reintegration windows.
- Provide observability hooks (per-tenant reintegration timeline, reason logs, health score) for Console and Alerting.

NON-GOALS
- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity planning or quota pricing changes.
- We will not change underlying scheduler allocation semantics in this iteration — keep to orchestration + autoscaler signals.

KEY CONCEPTS
- Reintegration Window: a time-bounded period after a tenant exits quarantine/soft-eviction during which their traffic is rate-limited and monitored. Default: 10 minutes. Configurable up to 2 hours for enterprise customers.

- Reintegration Mode (tenant-level):
  - conservative: slow ramp, strict health gating, mandatory warm prefetch.
  - balanced: medium ramp, health gating for tail latencies only.
  - aggressive: immediate full traffic, used only for high-SLA paying tenants.

- Tenant Health Score: rolling composite of p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, token churn (cache miss ratio), and recent evictions. Score in 0–100. Thresholds map to gating rules.

- Shear Window: short interval (e.g., 30s) used to smooth resource reallocation across tenants entering/leaving reintegration. Prevents all tenants rejoining at the same instant.

- Reintegration Queue: backend orchestration queue that sequences reintegration attempts and records audit events. Keeps backoff state for tenants (exponential backoff on repeated failures).

- Autoscaler Handoff Signal: a small surface to inform the autoscaler that this tenant is 'probationary' so that scale-ups for the pool prefer warm-pool capacity and avoid immediate preemption of other tenants.

API/Config CHANGES (small, targeted)
- Customer-visible: new optional field on dedicated pool config: reintegration_mode: {conservative|balanced|aggressive} and reintegration_max_window_minutes: int.
- Operator-visible: per-tenant override in Console with audit note.
- Internal signals: reintegration_state {queued|in_progress|succeeded|deferred|failed} exposed in telemetry.

OBSERVABILITY
- Console: Reintegration timeline chart per tenant (events: quarantine_start, quarantine_end, reintegration_start, gate_checks, reintegration_complete).
- Alerts: Reintegration-failure-rate > 5% across pool over 1h -> p1 to SRE on-call.
- Metrics to add: tenant_reintegration_attempts_total, tenant_reintegration_failures_total, tenant_health_score_gauge, reintegration_duration_seconds, reintegration_backoff_count.

AUTOSCALER INTERACTION
- Autoscaler receives 'probation' flag for tenants currently in reintegration. Handoff semantics: prefer warm-pool scaling and warm-instance reuse for probationary traffic; avoid immediate slab evictions.
- Prevents autoscaler from auto-decommitting warm instances brought up specifically for probationary tenants for at least reintegration_max_window_minutes.

OPERATIONAL FLOW (sketch)
1) Detection: Tenant triggers noisy behavior -> scheduler quarantines (soft-evict) tenant with reason tag. Quarantine_end event logged when conditions resolve or operator manually releases.
2) Enqueue: post-quarantine, tenant inserted into Reintegration Queue with chosen reintegration_mode.
3) Precheck: run health-score check; if score below precheck threshold, defer reintegration and schedule backoff.
4) Warm-prefetch: if mode != aggressive, request autoscaler to provision warm pool slots and prefetch KV/caches for tenant fingerprint.
5) Sheared ramp: release traffic in small increments (shear windows). Monitor health and tail latency; if health degrades, mark deferred and escalate.
6) Completion: after window and sustained healthy metrics, mark succeeded and remove probation tag.

EXPERIMENTS / SIMULATION PLAN
- Build synthetic noisy-neighbor scenarios (replay traces) and 3 candidate reintegration policies. Measure oscillation frequency, avg latency delta, and warm-start cost.
- Run A/B across canary dedicated pool (5% of traffic) for 4 weeks. Targets: 50% fewer oscillations, <=5% cost increase for prefetch.

ROLLOUT & ROLLBACK
- Phase 0: implement signals + telemetry in a canary environment. Validate metric correctness.
- Phase 1: enable in one region with conservative default; integrate with autoscaler warm-pool logic.
- Phase 2: allow tenant-level overrides for beta customers, collect feedback.
- Rollback: global toggle to disable reintegration orchestration and revert tenants to immediate rejoin behavior.

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE NOTES
- Reintegration audit events are persisted with tenant id and operator note — ensure retention complies with customer contracts.
- No customer data should be prefetched beyond cached model keys and KV fingerprints; avoid any PII pre-warming.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS TO MAKE
- What is the default reintegration_max_window_minutes? (Proposal: 10 minutes for balanced)
- Should reintegration health score incorporate model-quality signals (coherence/regression) or limit to infra metrics? (Start infra-only; add model-quality later)
- How granular should shearing be? (30s vs 2m)
- Should we expose reintegration analytics in Optimize as a cost/quality tradeoff?

TO-DOs (near term)
- [Sofia] Draft autoscaler handoff spec for eng-serving-runtime (PRD -> engineering).
- [Liam] Prototype reintegration queue with simple backoff in staging.
- [Aisha] Wire up tenant_health_score metric and console visualization mock.
- [Marcus] Create simulation traces (noisy neighbor) and baseline the current oscillation rate.

NOTES / DISCUSSION FRAGMENTS
- "Prefer warm pool reuse instead of spinning new machines when reintegrating" — reduces churn and prevents evictions from propagating.
- "Backoff must be exponential but bounded" — otherwise a tenant could be permanently delayed for months; propose cap at 2 hours with operator override.
- "We need clear UX for customers so they understand why their traffic is in probation" — Console should show short explanation + link to docs.

LINKS / REFERENCES
- Related tickets: DED-873 (reintegration queue prototype), PROD-1245 (warm-pool autoscaler changes)
- Observability spec: Capacity Observability Spec (Confluence)

END — this is intentionally sketchy, looking for feedback on the high-level orchestration and the autoscaler handoff semantics.

Version notes: first draft, 2025-11-03. Last updated with simulation plan and autoscaler handoff sketch 2026-02-25.
